record.paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures on Rational Systems in Three Dimensions
record.context_brief: stability and periodicity in bounded cases
record.original_question: For every special case of the three-dimensional rational system x_{n+1} = (alpha_1 + beta_1 x_n + gamma_1 y_n + delta_1 z_n)/(A_1 + B_1 x_n + C_1 y_n + D_1 z_n), y_{n+1} = (alpha_2 + beta_2 x_n + gamma_2 y_n + delta_2 z_n)/(A_2 + B_2 x_n + C_2 y_n + D_2 z_n), and z_{n+1} = (alpha_3 + beta_3 x_n + gamma_3 y_n + delta_3 z_n)/(A_3 + B_3 x_n + C_3 y_n + D_3 z_n), with nonnegative parameters, nonnegative initial conditions, positive denominators, and bounded solutions, what are the global stability properties of its equilibrium points and the periodic nature of its solutions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the three-dimensional system of rational difference equations
\[
x_{n+1} = \frac{\alpha_1 + \beta_1 x_n + \gamma_1 y_n + \delta_1 z_n}{A_1 + B_1 x_n + C_1 y_n + D_1 z_n}, \quad y_{n+1} = \frac{\alpha_2 + \beta_2 x_n + \gamma_2 y_n + \delta_2 z_n}{A_2 + B_2 x_n + C_2 y_n + D_2 z_n}, \quad z_{n+1} = \frac{\alpha_3 + \beta_3 x_n + \gamma_3 y_n + \delta_3 z_n}{A_3 + B_3 x_n + C_3 y_n + D_3 z_n},
\]
where all parameters \(\alpha_i,\beta_i,\gamma_i,\delta_i,A_i,B_i,C_i,D_i\) (\(i=1,2,3\)) are nonnegative real numbers, and the initial conditions \((x_0,y_0,z_0)\) are nonnegative. Assume that for every \(n \ge 0\) the three denominators are strictly positive and the resulting trajectory \((x_n,y_n,z_n)\) is bounded.

A "special case" of this system is obtained by fixing some of the 24 parameters to be zero and keeping the others positive (so that each particular numerator/denominator structure is a specific choice among the \(2^{24}\) possible parameter-support patterns, restricted to those for which every solution is bounded).

For each such special case:
(a) Determine all nonnegative equilibrium points \((\bar x,\bar y,\bar z)\) of the system and decide, for each equilibrium, whether it is locally asymptotically stable, globally asymptotically stable (attracting every nonnegative initial condition with positive denominators), unstable, or a saddle.
(b) Describe the periodic character of solutions: identify all minimal periods that arise, determine whether nontrivial periodic solutions exist, and, when they do, characterize the set of initial conditions producing them.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem belongs to a broad program of classifying the dynamics of rational systems in three dimensions; the two-dimensional analogue (Camouzis-Ladas-Kulenovic et al.) has been studied case-by-case over many years and remains incomplete, and the three-dimensional case introduces hundreds of subcases. No comprehensive resolution is known; individual special cases continue to be analyzed in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems and Conjectures on Rational Systems in Three Dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Open problems and conjectures concerning the global behavior of three-dimensional rational systems.
status_evidence.claim: The questions on stability and periodicity for these 3D rational systems are posed as open problems and conjectures.
